questions: Can you confirm if there have been any changes to your medication list since your last hospital visit, particularly regarding any acid-reducing medications?

events.value: blood pressure one hundred sixty over one hundred

preop_note_claims: Patient has a history of Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), and Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 3).

Current medications include Metformin 500mg twice daily, Lisinopril 10mg once daily, Amlodipine 5mg once daily, Dutasteride 0.5mg once daily, and Aspirin 75mg once daily. Omeprazole 20mg once daily was discontinued 6 months ago due to resolution of gastritis; patient now uses Pantoprazole 30mg once daily as needed.
Patient has a known allergy to Penicillin.
ASA-PS is 3 due to the presence of controlled comorbidities including Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, and Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 3).

Airway assessment indicates no anticipated difficulties; anesthesia plan includes General Anesthesia with Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia for elective Prostatectomy (Transurethral Resection of the Prostate, TURP).
handoff_claims: Patient has a history of Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), and Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 3) which may impact recovery and fluid management.
Intraoperative course was uncomplicated with Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia; anticipate potential for residual spinal anesthetic effects and monitor for hypotension or urinary retention in PACU.
Anticipated issues include potential for postoperative bleeding, need for ongoing blood pressure and glucose control, and monitoring of renal function due to Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 3).
distractors: History of pneumonia resolved 2 years ago
Remote history of left femur fracture (30 years ago), fully healed
Previous use of Warfarin for atrial fibrillation, discontinued 4 years ago
